missionPremise: P-124 (Central Texas completion sprint) reversed A-027's 'one bake; do not rebake' for this sprint -- the factory-bastrop-publish bake (25 executions 2026-08-28..2026-08-30, all six CTX counties published) will run again. completionPredicate: Per the WDLL card (_inbox/2026-09-07_ctx-f_WDLL.md), reproduced in compressed form: (1) a pre-bake per-county/per-rail gate is wired into runBastropPublish for both targets, proven to refuse by a unit test seeding a deliberately unaccounted rail; (2) factory-staging-reset's Cloud Run template carries live-rederived Neon project/branch ids, no execution-time override needed; (3) staging-reset's own run also rotates the two STAGING_* Secret Manager secrets to the new branch hosts, pooler refused; (4) STAGING_SIBLING_SQL's staleness has a named, tested bound with its own refusal code; (5) the LDT pin bump decision (bump vs. hold) is evidence-backed by an actual transitive-closure diff, not the dispatch's own unverified framing; (6) the tier2-conformant stub cannot run in this bake by default, without deleting the capability; (7) the two record-only facts (no bake serialization; counts-only run record) are named in the close with their file/line evidence, not built into a fix unless one falls out of the above for free.
scopeBasis: Repo hauska-factory only, this worktree only. Do not touch doc_repo except the three checkpoint files this dispatch names (CP1/CP2/CLOSE) -- I commit my own repo, doc_repo commits are not mine to make. Do not overlap CTX-G's county_facet_coverage / ledger rails, CTX-C's cadRoll rail definitions, or CTX-D's geometry/footprint absence definitions -- I consume parcel_gate_verdict (already-landed, F-01 PARCEL-B-GATE-SCHED contract) as the readiness instrument rather than inventing a second one, per the program's own CTRL-1 lesson (one rule, one data source). No production bake, no production deploy, no traffic shift -- everything here is code + tests + template/config changes that a human or a later, explicitly-authorized execution turns on.

findingsBeforeBuild.finding: No per-county/per-rail readiness gate exists anywhere in the bake/publish path today (confirmed by reading src/jobs/bastrop-publish.mjs runBastropPublish in full: its only pre-bake checks are dry-run, OPERATOR_PUBLISH_GO, target-env resolution, and the staging-sibling/branch-fresh checks -- none touch rail_absence, county_rail, county_facet_coverage, or parcel_gate_verdict). The instrument the dispatch wants already exists in a different, unwired form: migration 0009 + src/jobs/publish-gate-sched.mjs already define parcel_gate_verdict (county_fips, rail_key) -> verdict IN (pass, refuse, excluded), unaccounted_count, written by a SEPARATE scheduled Cloud Run job (factory-publish-gate-sched) that never runs as part of, or gates, bastrop-publish.mjs. It exists today purely to feed a serve-side LDT allowlist (parcelGateVerdictRead.ts / PARCEL-B-READER), not the bake. Reusing it as the pre-bake instrument (rather than building a second parallel readiness concept against rail_absence/county_rail) is a deliberate design choice: it is already the program's own definition of 'this rail is either populated or a declared absence' at (county, rail) grain, with unaccounted_count already meaning exactly what item 1 calls 'unaccounted'.

publish-gate-sched.mjs's DEFAULT_SCHED_RAIL_KEYS is built from five named slate constants (SLATE_1/1B/1C/1D + LANDUSE_OWNER_GATE_GAP), each with its own dated module-doc justifying why it was added and confirming (per its own comments) that adding it was verified safe first. Its own comment is explicit: 'do not add to this constant; add to SLATE_1B_RAIL_KEYS below instead' -- i.e. this is already the program's single source of truth for 'the full known rail set', extended by convention rather than ad hoc. Building the readiness gate to default to this same list (rather than re-deriving a second rail universe) means CTX-C/CTX-D/CTX-G's future rail-key contributions land in one place and both the scheduler and this gate inherit them automatically -- the alternative (a second hardcoded list here) is exactly the CTRL-1 divergence shape DEV_PROCESS 2.4 names.

setbackFrontFt is a named counter-example already on record in publish-gate-sched.mjs's own comments: it is declared in rail-keys.js and referenced by the allowlist but has NO writer on this branch, so gating on it would make every county permanently refuse (DEV_PROCESS 2.0's dead-gate trap) while never being actionable. It is correctly excluded from DEFAULT_SCHED_RAIL_KEYS today. This lane inherits that exclusion by reusing the constant rather than re-litigating it.

cloudbuild.publish.yaml:75 confirms the dispatch's claim exactly: the factory-staging-reset job's deployed template carries only FACTORY_DATABASE_URL and NEON_API_KEY as secrets, and no --set-env-vars or --set-secrets entry for any of the four *_NEON_PROJECT_ID / *_NEON_PARENT_BRANCH_ID names src/jobs/staging-reset.mjs requires. staging-reset.mjs's own throw on a missing var has no .code, so the recorded runs.refuse_code is always the generic STAGING_RESET_FAILED rather than a specific missing-env code (unlike publish-target-env.mjs's TARGET_ENV_MISSING pattern) -- a secondary, smaller finding worth fixing alongside the main one since it currently hides which of the four vars is actually missing from anyone reading the runs table.

src/db/connect.mjs's refusePoolerHost only guards connectFactory (i.e. FACTORY_DATABASE_URL). The bake's own STAGING_NEONDB_URL / STAGING_HAUSKA_MCP_URL values are read directly as bake subprocess env (publish-target-env.mjs resolveTargetStores) with no pooler check on that path at all -- so a rotation script that ever wrote a pooler host into those two secrets would ship it straight into the bake with nothing catching it. neon-branches.mjs's createBranchFromParent already refuses a pooler host in the branch-creation response itself, which covers branch creation, but NOT a rotation step that separately calls Neon's connection_uri endpoint to obtain a full credentialed URI (a different Neon API response shape) -- that call site needs its own pooler check before writing to Secret Manager.

findingsBeforeBuild.finding: Confirmed by direct read: src/lib/publish-guards.mjs's STAGING_SIBLING_SQL has ORDER BY pr.completed_at DESC NULLS LAST, pr.created_at DESC LIMIT 1 with no WHERE clause bounding completed_at at all -- exactly as the dispatch describes. evaluateStagingSibling (same file) already has a deliberate one-code-per-failure-reason design (STAGING_SIBLING_REQUIRED / _UNWALKED / _FAILED / _NO_SWEEP each independently provable by fixture per its own module doc) -- a recency bound should get its own code in the same style (STAGING_SIBLING_STALE) rather than being folded into the SQL's WHERE clause, which would collapse 'no sibling ever' and 'sibling exists but is stale' into the same STAGING_SIBLING_REQUIRED code and lose exactly the diagnostic distinction this module was built to preserve.

The nodeFacetBakeTier2ConformantCli.ts file itself lives only in the external LDT repo (not checked into hauska-factory), so its {flood:null,...} / PLACE_COORD_SENTINEL literals could not be quoted from this repo directly; the exclusion point is entirely on the hauska-factory side (the call site), which is sufficient to stop it running regardless of what the LDT-side file contains.

design.readinessGate: New file src/lib/publish-readiness-gate.mjs, same module-doc convention as publish-guards.mjs (Executes/Triggers/Fails/Bypasses). Pure function evaluatePreBakeReadiness(rows, requiredRails) built for fixture-only testing (mirrors evaluateStagingSibling's shape): for each rail in requiredRails, no matching row -> throw RAIL_UNACCOUNTED naming the rail; row.verdict === 'refuse' -> throw RAIL_REFUSED naming the rail and its unaccounted_count; 'pass' or 'excluded' -> counted ok. Thin wrapper requirePreBakeReadiness(client, countyFips, requiredRails = DEFAULT_SCHED_RAIL_KEYS imported from ../jobs/publish-gate-sched.mjs) runs `SELECT county_fips, rail_key, verdict, unaccounted_count, evaluated_at FROM parcel_gate_verdict WHERE county_fips = $1 AND rail_key = ANY($2::text[])` and calls the pure evaluator. Wired into runBastropPublish immediately after resolveTargetStores, before the target-branch/sibling branch and before any bake call, for BOTH staging and production (a bad-data staging bake would poison its own sibling walk and then satisfy Rule 6 for a production publish on the same incomplete data, so gating only production would be a hole).
design.stagingTemplate: Add the four *_NEON_PROJECT_ID / *_NEON_PARENT_BRANCH_ID values to the factory-staging-reset case in cloudbuild.publish.yaml's EXTRA_ENV (plain --set-env-vars, not secrets -- they are opaque ids, not credentials, matching how CLOUD_RUN_REGION/CONTRACT_VERSION are already handled). Values re-derived live via the Neon API against the actual current project/branch state, not copied from the 11-day-old recorded pair. Also give staging-reset.mjs's per-prefix throw a .code (STAGING_RESET_ENV_MISSING, naming which prefix) so a future failure is legible in runs.refuse_code instead of the generic STAGING_RESET_FAILED.
design.secretRotation: Extend runStagingReset (src/jobs/staging-reset.mjs) so that after the staging_targets UPSERT succeeds, it derives a full connection string per store (Neon connection_uri endpoint or equivalent, reusing the existing role/db already in use for that store -- exact mechanism pending the Neon recon sub-agent's findings) and writes new Secret Manager versions for STAGING_NEONDB_URL and STAGING_HAUSKA_MCP_URL, refusing (reusing refusePoolerHost from src/db/connect.mjs) if either resolved host is a pooler host. This closes the loop the dispatch names: the bake reads these two secrets via `:latest`, so the next bastrop-publish execution picks up the new branch automatically with no hand step.
design.siblingRecency: Add MAX_SIBLING_AGE_HOURS (exported constant, documented default -- exact value to be chosen against real bake duration data: bastrop-publish's own Cloud Run timeout is 6h, so the bound must clear a single legitimate run comfortably while still catching a multi-day-old sibling) to src/lib/publish-guards.mjs. evaluateStagingSibling gains a new early check (after the 'no row' check, before unwalked/failed/sweep) computing the row's age against `now` (injectable for tests, matching requireBranchFresh's own style) and throwing STAGING_SIBLING_STALE naming the row's age and the bound when exceeded. STAGING_SIBLING_SQL itself is left unbounded (still finds the true most-recent row) so the distinct 'stale' reason stays legible rather than collapsing into STAGING_SIBLING_REQUIRED.
design.pinBump: Held pending the LDT closure-diff sub-agent. If the transitive closure (not just the four entry files) is confirmed unchanged in substance, bump _LDT_SHA and _CONTRACT_VERSION in cloudbuild.publish.yaml with the diff evidence named in the close. If anything material changed, the pin stays and the finding is reported to doc-repo-26 instead.
design.tier2Exclusion: Add an explicit, default-false flag (e.g. flags.includeTier2ConformantStub, wired through parsePublishFlags as an opt-in CLI flag, never a template default) gating the existing invokeLdtBake('node-facet-bake-tier2-conformant', ...) call inside runChunkedConformantBakes. When skipped, tier2Summary reports {written: 0, pages: pages.length, skipped: true, skipReason: '...'} rather than a bare zero, so a future reader cannot misread a deliberate skip as a failed run (DEV_PROCESS 4.3: an empty result is not an absence, and the reverse -- a deliberate skip must not read as an empty/failed result either). The bundling entry in scripts/build-publish-bake-clis.mjs and BAKE_CLI_FILES stay as-is (capability preserved, not deleted) since retiring tier2 outright is named in the dispatch as an operator ruling, not this lane's to make; the retirement question itself goes to doc-repo-26 in this lane's close as a flagged, undecided finding.
design.recordOnlyItems: No code built for item 6 (write-slot serialization; parcel-level run naming) unless something falls out of the above work for free. Recorded in the close with exact file:line evidence (src/jobs/bastrop-publish.mjs never calls src/control/leases.mjs; recordBakePageEvent's body carries counts only, never a prop_id list).

preRegisteredFalsifiers: If a unit test seeding one required rail as verdict='refuse' does NOT cause runBastropPublish to throw before bakesFn is ever called (spy count 0), item 1 is not met.
If a required rail with zero parcel_gate_verdict rows for the county is treated as passing rather than refused, item 1's 'unaccounted is fatal at publish' half is not met.

If the readiness gate silently converts an existing 'refuse' row into a passing state anywhere in this lane's own code (rather than only reading the verdict column), that is exactly the relabelling the dispatch's WATCH FOR warns against -- pre-registered as a defect if found in review.

If factory-staging-reset's template change still requires an --update-env-vars override for a plain `gcloud run jobs execute` to succeed (checked by reading the deployed template's env/secrets after the yaml change is written, not by assuming the yaml edit alone is sufficient -- an actual redeploy is out of this lane's scope per 'no production deploy', so this will be verified as far as static template correctness allows, and named as unverified-live in the close if a real deploy is required to fully confirm).
If the secret-rotation code path ever writes a host containing '-pooler' to Secret Manager without throwing first, item 2's rotation half is not met.
If evaluateStagingSibling still returns a sibling whose completed_at is older than MAX_SIBLING_AGE_HOURS without throwing STAGING_SIBLING_STALE, item 3 is not met.

If _LDT_SHA is bumped without a real closure diff attached as evidence in the close (i.e. bumped on the dispatch's own unverified claim alone), item 4 is not met regardless of whether the bump happens to be safe.
If tier2-conformant still runs when flags.includeTier2ConformantStub is left at its default, item 5 is not met.
If node --test after all changes reports fail > 1 beyond the pre-existing flaky heartbeat test (re-verified in isolation), something in this lane's own change broke the suite.
